title: Your family

segments.voice: Yesterday, your character. Your line: one trait. Did you take a moment last night to see where your trait showed up, and where it slipped? The first place a trait gets tested is usually home. Today, home. Day one thousand four hundred eight.

A man named al-Aswad put a plain question to Aisha: what did the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, do at home? Not in the mosque, not leading anyone. At home. Her answer, in Sahih al-Bukhari: he would be busy serving his family, and when the time for prayer came, he would go out to pray. That's the whole report. No miracle in it. A man helping around the house, then stopping for prayer. It is a strangely ordinary thing to have been remembered. Today, practice at home, with family.
screen: `WHAT DID HE DO AT HOME?` → `SERVING HIS FAMILY.` → `THEN, THE PRAYER.`

segments.voice: Start with that report, because it sets the order of things. Service at home and prayer are not rivals. The same person does both, in the same afternoon. Next, the house itself. In another hadith in Bukhari, the Prophet tells his followers to pray some of their prayers in their houses, and not to make their houses like graves. The picture is stark: a house with no prayer in it is likened to a grave. Third, praying together. When people pray together, one can lead and the others stand behind in a row. A parent leads, a child stands beside or behind, and the prayer is said at the same pace. Small children wander in and out of it; in Bukhari there's a report of the Prophet praying while carrying his little granddaughter Umamah, setting her down when he went down in prostration and picking her up when he stood. The tradition did not wait for a quiet house to pray in one. Last, families as they really are. Some homes are all Muslim. Some have a new Muslim and parents who aren't. Some have a spouse from another faith or none. Praying together can mean one person praying while another sits nearby in quiet, or a family sharing a meal and saying bismillah before it. In surah Ta Ha, Allah tells the Prophet to bid his household to prayer and to be patient in it. Patient is the word to keep. Habits at home grow slowly, and nobody is helped by being pushed.
screen: `SERVICE AT HOME, THEN PRAYER.` · `DON'T MAKE YOUR HOUSE A GRAVE.` · `ONE LEADS, A CHILD BESIDE.` · `FAMILIES AS THEY REALLY ARE.`

segments.voice: The practice: pray together once. First, a quiet minute here. Breathe slowly. Bring to mind the people you live with, or the family you're closest to, one face at a time. Notice where each of them is right now, this hour. Let one small act of service come to mind for one of them: a dish washed, a bag carried, a phone call returned. Hold it. If you pray, you can choose one prayer today and invite someone at home to stand with you for it, simply, without a speech. If you don't pray, or your family doesn't, you could share one quiet moment at a meal instead. After the bell, do the act of service first, then the prayer or the pause. The bell holds the time.
Your family. The first place practice is lived: serving at home, and praying there too. Today's word.
Your line: pray together. Today, do one small chore for someone at home before they ask, and say nothing about it. Tomorrow, your neighbor. Day one thousand four hundred eight.

howItsDone: Muslim families may pray some prayers together at home, with one person leading and the others standing behind in a row and children joining as they learn, following the hadith that encourages praying some prayers in the house.

fork.setup: you're about to pray, and your small granddaughter won't let go of you. what did the Prophet do?
options: prayed while carrying her, setting her down to prostrate.
sent her out of the room.
fork.reveal: Sahih al-Bukhari tells of him praying while carrying Umamah, setting her down when he went down in prostration and picking her up when he stood.

original.note: Arabic: family, household, a person's people.

trapdoor: what you thought: religious practice happens at the mosque, and home is time off.
what it means: home is the first place of practice: serving the family, and praying there too.
what a scholar hears: Aisha's report of the Prophet serving his family, the hadith against houses like graves, Umamah carried in prayer, and Ta Ha's command to be patient.

notes: Confirm Sahih al-Bukhari 676 (serving his family, going out at prayer time), 432 (pray in your houses, don't make them graves) and 516 (praying while carrying Umamah).
Umamah is the daughter of Zaynab, the Prophet's daughter; 'his little granddaughter' should be checked.
The hook names al-Aswad as the one who asked Aisha (Sahih al-Bukhari 676); confirm.
The section on mixed-faith families should be checked for a welcoming, accurate tone; 'saying bismillah before a meal' is described, not required.

Editor: Sahih al-Bukhari 516 says he set Umamah down when he prostrated, not when he bowed; fixed in the teach, myth, fork option and reveal. Replaced the gloss on the houses-like-graves hadith with the hadith's own picture, and dropped the count in 'two or more people'.
